rows.expectedResultText: White or almost white solid with a waxy or paraffin-like appearance.
Very soluble in water and in methylene chloride, practically insoluble in alcohol, in fatty oils and in mineral oils.

rows.expectedResultText: An abundant, white, crystalline precipitate is formed.

tests.procedure: Under strong white light check each received sample container separately on a clean transparent watch glass or glass dish for foreign particles, colour and conformity with the visual specification.
tests.source: Polyethylen Glycol 6000__STM Polyethylen Glycol after edit (no equipments).txt:28

tests.procedure: BP-style stepwise solubility: 100 mg sample in a stoppered tube with 0.1 mL solvent, shake 1 min, hold 25.0 ± 0.5 °C for 15 min (repeat once if not dissolved); add 0.9 mL, then 2 mL, then 7 mL solvent with the same shake and hold to classify very soluble / freely soluble / soluble / sparingly soluble; if still undissolved, 10 mg in 10 mL (slightly soluble), then 1 mg in 10 mL (very slightly soluble), else practically insoluble. Repeat with methylene chloride, ethanol (96 per cent), dilute nitric acid and dilute hydrochloric acid.

solvents: first solvent not named in the STM (see openQuestions)
details.reference: BP (SC IV K.) Characters Section in Monographs (Hygroscopicity and Solubility)

tests.source: Polyethylen Glycol 6000__STM Polyethylen Glycol after edit (no equipments).txt:29

tests.procedure: Identification test 1 (BP 2024 Macrogols): to 1 g in a test tube add 0.5 mL sulfuric acid; close with a stopper fitted with a bent delivery tube; heat until white fumes evolve; collect the fumes through the delivery tube into 1 mL mercuric chloride solution. An abundant white crystalline precipitate forms.

details.collectionSolution: 1 mL mercury chloride solution (5.4 g mercuric chloride to 100 mL water)

tests.source: Polyethylen Glycol 6000__STM Polyethylen Glycol after edit (no equipments).txt:30; reagent Polyethylen Glycol 6000__STM Polyethylen Glycol after edit (no equipments).txt:26

tests.procedure: Identification test 2 (BP 2024 Macrogols): to 0.1 g add 0.1 g potassium thiocyanate and 0.1 g cobalt nitrate; mix thoroughly with a glass rod; add 5 mL methylene chloride and shake. The liquid phase becomes blue.
tests.source: Polyethylen Glycol 6000__STM Polyethylen Glycol after edit (no equipments).txt:30

tests.procedure: Appearance of solution (BP 2024 Appendix IV B): dissolve 12.5 g in water to 50 mL; the solution must be clear and not more intensely coloured than reference solution BY6. Standard solution BY: 2.4 mL yellow solution, 1.0 mL red solution and 0.4 mL blue solution with 6.2 mL hydrochloric acid (10 g/L). Reference solution BY6: 5.0 mL standard solution BY with 95.0 mL hydrochloric acid (10 g/L).

details.standardSolutionBY: 2.4 mL yellow + 1.0 mL red + 0.4 mL blue solution + 6.2 mL hydrochloric acid (10 g/L)
details.referenceSolutionBY6: 5.0 mL standard solution BY + 95.0 mL hydrochloric acid (10 g/L)

tests.source: Polyethylen Glycol 6000__STM Polyethylen Glycol after edit (no equipments).txt:31; reagents Polyethylen Glycol 6000__STM Polyethylen Glycol after edit (no equipments).txt:26

tests.procedure: Acidity or alkalinity (BP 2024): dissolve 5.0 g in 50 mL carbon dioxide-free water; add 0.15 mL bromothymol blue solution R1; the solution is yellow or green. Limit: not more than 0.1 mL of 0.1 M sodium hydroxide is required to change the colour of the indicator to blue. (The STM does not describe the titration step; see openQuestions.)
tests.source: Polyethylen Glycol 6000__STM Polyethylen Glycol after edit (no equipments).txt:32

tests.procedure: Viscosity (BP 2024 Appendix V H, macrogols with relative molecular mass above 400): weigh 50 g sample, add 50 mL water, dissolve well to give a 50% m/m solution; measure with a calibrated rotational viscometer.
tests.source: Polyethylen Glycol 6000__STM Polyethylen Glycol after edit (no equipments).txt:33

tests.procedure: Freezing point (BP 2024 Appendix V B): place a sufficient amount of sample in a Nessler tube; insert the thermometer without touching the bottom of the tube; heat carefully and record the freezing temperature; or use a freezing point apparatus in the same way.

details.apparatus: Nessler tube with thermometer, or freezing point apparatus

tests.source: Polyethylen Glycol 6000__STM Polyethylen Glycol after edit (no equipments).txt:34

tests.procedure: Reducing substances (BP 2024): dissolve 1 g in 1 mL of a 10 g/L resorcinol solution, warm gently if necessary; add 2 mL hydrochloric acid; after 5 min the solution must not be more intensely coloured than reference solution R3. Standard solution R: 1.0 mL yellow solution + 2.0 mL red solution + 7.0 mL hydrochloric acid (10 g/L). Reference solution R3: 50.0 mL standard solution R + 50.0 mL hydrochloric acid (10 g/L).

details.standardSolutionR: 1.0 mL yellow + 2.0 mL red solution + 7.0 mL hydrochloric acid (10 g/L)
details.referenceSolutionR3: 50.0 mL standard solution R + 50.0 mL hydrochloric acid (10 g/L)

tests.source: Polyethylen Glycol 6000__STM Polyethylen Glycol after edit (no equipments).txt:35

tests.procedure: Water (BP 2024 Appendix IX C): determined on 2.00 g with a calibrated Karl Fischer apparatus.
tests.source: Polyethylen Glycol 6000__STM Polyethylen Glycol after edit (no equipments).txt:36

tests.procedure: Sulphated ash (BP Appendix IX A): weigh an empty crucible previously ignited at 600 ± 50 °C and cooled in desiccator (W0); weigh accurately 1.0 g into a platinum crucible (W1); moisten with about 1 mL sulfuric acid, heat gently until thoroughly charred; moisten the residue again with sulfuric acid and heat until white fumes are no longer evolved; ignite in a calibrated muffle at 600 ± 50 °C until completely incinerated, cool in desiccator and weigh (W2); repeat to constant weight. % = (W2 - W0) / (W1 - W0) x 100.
tests.source: Polyethylen Glycol 6000__STM Polyethylen Glycol after edit (no equipments).txt:37

openQuestions.question: Microbiology: TAMC, TYMC and E. coli limits appear only in the spec sheet. The STM has no microbiological examination section, so no procedure is transcribed. Confirm the procedure and SOP.
openQuestions.source: Polyethylen Glycol 6000__Specifications sheet Polyethylen Glycol.txt:22-24; Polyethylen Glycol 6000__STM Polyethylen Glycol after edit (no equipments).txt:28-37

openQuestions.question: Solubility: the STM does not name the first solvent (it repeats with methylene chloride, ethanol, dilute nitric and dilute hydrochloric acid). The spec sheet lists water first and also fatty and mineral oils, which the STM does not test. Confirm.
openQuestions.source: Polyethylen Glycol 6000__STM Polyethylen Glycol after edit (no equipments).txt:29; Polyethylen Glycol 6000__Specifications sheet Polyethylen Glycol.txt:12

openQuestions.question: Acidity or alkalinity: the STM gives the sample preparation and indicator but no titration with 0.1 M sodium hydroxide, which the spec limit depends on. Limit loaded as a Measurement (mL); confirm the titration step.
openQuestions.source: Polyethylen Glycol 6000__STM Polyethylen Glycol after edit (no equipments).txt:32; Polyethylen Glycol 6000__Specifications sheet Polyethylen Glycol.txt:16

openQuestions.question: Viscosity: spindle, rotational speed and measuring temperature are not stated. Method details needed before the result can be reproduced.
